claims.text: Applying a nanocrystalline TiAlN coating by PVD will improve surface hardness relative to an untreated metallic surface.
Applying a nanocrystalline TiAlN coating by PVD will improve wear resistance relative to an untreated metallic surface.
Applying a nanocrystalline TiAlN coating by PVD will improve oxidation resistance relative to an untreated metallic surface.
The proposed intervention is a TiAlN coating approximately 3 µm thick deposited using PVD.
PVD deposition will produce a dense, adherent nanocrystalline ceramic layer over the substrate.
The TiAlN layer will act as a physical barrier that reduces substrate oxidation.
The TiAlN layer will act as a physical barrier that reduces substrate corrosion.
The high hardness of the TiAlN coating will minimize the initiation of surface microcracks under mechanical stress.
The high hardness of the TiAlN coating will minimize the propagation of surface microcracks under mechanical stress.
Reduced oxidation, corrosion, and microcracking will diminish wear rates.
Reduced oxidation, corrosion, and microcracking will improve surface integrity.
The coating will retain its improved properties at temperatures up to approximately 600°C in corrosive and abrasive environments.
Coating stability beyond approximately 600°C is not guaranteed.
The general benefits of PVD-deposited ceramic coatings are well documented.
The exact percentage increase in hardness and reduction in wear under the specified conditions is uncertain without targeted experiments.
